lines.text: Inside each motor, a magnet spins past coils of wire. Spin one by hand, and it makes electricity. Every motor is also a generator.
So while it spins, it pushes voltage back against the battery. That's called back E M F.
The faster it spins, the harder it pushes back. Less current flows, so the shaft gets less twist, called torque.
At top speed, the push-back matches the battery's twelve volts. No current flows, so there's no push left at all.
It's like a playground merry-go-round. Standing still, you can shove it hard. Spinning fast, your hands can barely keep up.
So at low speed, the tires are the limit. Near top speed, the motors are.
Braking is different. There, back E M F helps instead of fighting, so only grip limits braking.
